breakfast.name: Menemen (Turkish Scrambled Eggs with Peppers)
ingredients: Green peppers (Turkish long green peppers -- thin and mildly spicy)
Optional: sucuk (Turkish sausage) or pastirma (cured beef)
instructions: Menemen is the Turkish egg dish -- and the subject of a fierce national debate
The debate: should menemen have onion or not?
Onion camp: adds the onion before the peppers and tomatoes
No-onion camp: onion ruins the texture and flavor
This debate is taken seriously -- it has its own social media arguments in Turkey
The eggs: stirred in and scrambled loosely (not set)
Some prefer sucuk (Turkish spiced sausage) added
Eaten with fresh bread for dipping
breakfast.description: Turkish scrambled eggs with peppers and tomatoes -- the subject of Turkey's great culinary debate (onion vs no-onion). Long green peppers and ripe tomatoes cooked in olive oil, eggs stirred in and kept soft. The onion question divides families. Eaten with bread for dipping. A Turkish breakfast staple.

breakfast.name: Simit (Sesame Bread Ring)
ingredients: Grape molasses (pekmez -- for the sesame coating glaze)
instructions: Simit is the Turkish sesame bread ring -- the street food of Istanbul
Found everywhere: on carts pushed by simitci (simit sellers), at bakeries, at every corner
The dough is ring-shaped and dipped in diluted grape molasses (pekmez) before rolling in sesame seeds
The molasses gives the crust its characteristic deep golden color and slight sweetness
Baked until the sesame is toasty and the crust is crunchy
Eaten for breakfast with white cheese (beyaz peynir) and tea (cay)
The simitci with his tray on his head is the image of Istanbul street life
breakfast.description: Turkish sesame bread ring -- yeasted dough formed into a ring, dipped in diluted grape molasses (pekmez, which gives the golden crust and slight sweetness), rolled generously in sesame seeds, and baked. The street food of Istanbul, sold from carts by simitci vendors. Eaten with white cheese and tea.

breakfast.name: Gozleme (Stuffed Flatbread)
ingredients: Yufka or thin flatbread (or homemade dough rolled thin)
Spinach and white cheese filling OR ground beef and onion
instructions: Gozleme is the Turkish stuffed flatbread -- traditionally made by women on a sac (concave griddle)
A thin dough is rolled out, filled on one half, folded, and cooked on the sac
The most popular filling: spinach and beyaz peynir (white cheese)
Or ground beef with onion and peppers
Cooked in butter until golden and crispy
Sold at Turkish markets and roadside stalls -- the sac is visible
The sound of the dough being stretched on the sac is the sound of Turkish markets
breakfast.description: Turkish filled flatbread -- thin dough rolled on a sac (concave griddle), filled with spinach and white cheese (or ground beef), folded and cooked in butter until golden. Traditionally made by women at Turkish markets. The sac griddle and the stretching sound are the market experience.

breakfast.name: Turkish Breakfast Spread (Kahvalti)
instructions: Turkish breakfast (kahvalti) is a spread -- not a single dish
Kahvalti literally means under (before) coffee -- the word suggests it predates the first coffee
A mezze-style approach to breakfast: many small components
The spread: white cheese, olives, tomatoes, cucumber, honey with kaymak, jams, butter, eggs, and sucuk
Sucuk: the Turkish spiced dry sausage -- pan-fried until the fat renders and it sizzles
Kaymak: Turkish clotted cream, thicker than cream -- eaten with honey
Eaten slowly on weekends: kahvalti is a leisurely event in Turkey
breakfast.description: Turkish breakfast spread -- kahvalti (under coffee) is a spread of beyaz peynir (white brine cheese), olives, tomatoes, cucumber, honey with kaymak (clotted cream), jams, pan-fried sucuk (spiced sausage), and boiled eggs. A leisurely weekend event in Turkey. Mezze-style approach to the first meal.

lunch.name: Doner Kebab
ingredients: Lamb or beef (sliced thin, layered and compressed onto a vertical spit)
Marinade: yoghurt, olive oil, onion juice, spices (cumin, paprika, oregano, black pepper)
Tomato, onion, parsley, sumac (for the doner sandwich)
instructions: Doner kebab is Turkey's most internationally known food
Doner means rotating in Turkish -- the meat rotates on a vertical spit
The meat is layered in a cone shape, compressing as it rotates
The outer layer cooks while the inside stays raw -- sliced off continuously as needed
Invented in Bursa, Turkey in the 19th century (Iskender Efendi often credited)
Eaten in a flatbread wrap (the street version) or on a plate with rice and vegetables
The doner traveled to Germany with Turkish gastarbeiter (guest workers) in the 1960s
The German doner kebab is now Berlin's most popular fast food and a cultural institution
lunch.description: Turkish rotating spit-roasted lamb or beef -- meat stacked in a cone on a vertical rotating spit, outer layer sliced as it cooks. Invented in Bursa in the 19th century. Eaten in flatbread with tomato, onion, and sumac. Traveled to Germany with Turkish workers in the 1960s; the Berlin doner is now Germany's most eaten fast food.

lunch.name: Mercimek Corbasi (Red Lentil Soup)
ingredients: Butter (for the finishing drizzle with dried mint)
instructions: Mercimek corbasi is the Turkish red lentil soup -- ubiquitous across Turkey
Simple but deeply satisfying
The lentils cook down completely until smooth
Finished with a drizzle of butter sizzled with paprika and dried mint
The butter-paprika drizzle sizzles when it hits the soup
Lemon squeezed at the table
Eaten as a starter at virtually every Turkish meal
lunch.description: Turkish red lentil soup -- red lentils cooked until completely smooth, finished with a sizzling drizzle of butter with paprika and dried mint. Lemon at the table. Eaten as a starter at virtually every Turkish meal. The butter drizzle sizzle is the signature finishing moment.

lunch.name: Lahmacun (Turkish Flatbread with Minced Meat)
ingredients: Onion, tomato, peppers (all very finely chopped)
Parsley, onion, sumac (rolled inside as toppings)
instructions: Lahmacun is the Turkish thin flatbread with a spiced meat topping -- often called Turkish pizza overseas
But it predates modern pizza and is fundamentally different: very thin, no cheese
The dough is rolled paper-thin
The meat topping is finely minced with onion, tomato, herbs, and spices
Baked quickly in a very hot oven
Served with parsley, lemon, and sumac
Rolled up with the herbs inside to eat -- a wrap
Lahm bi-ajeen in Arabic (meat on dough) -- it also exists in Lebanon and Syria
lunch.description: Turkish thin flatbread with minced lamb -- lahmacun (from Arabic lahm bi-ajeen: meat on dough), paper-thin dough topped with finely spiced lamb-onion-tomato paste, baked in a very hot oven. No cheese. Rolled up with parsley and sumac to eat. Also exists in Lebanon and Syria.

lunch.name: Iskender Kebab
ingredients: Pide bread (torn into pieces -- the base)
Brown butter (poured hot over at serving)
instructions: Iskender kebab is a specific dish from Bursa -- named after Iskender Efendi, who is credited with inventing doner
Slices of doner meat placed on torn pide bread
Hot tomato sauce poured over
Then hot brown butter poured over -- it sizzles when it hits the tomato sauce and meat
Cold yoghurt on the side as contrast
The combination of hot butter, hot tomato sauce, meat, soggy bread, and cold yoghurt
Iskender kebab is not a street food -- it is a sit-down restaurant dish
lunch.description: Bursa-origin doner on soggy bread -- doner slices on torn pide bread, hot tomato sauce poured over, then sizzling brown butter poured over at the table. Cold yoghurt on the side. Named after Iskender Efendi (credited with inventing doner). A sit-down restaurant dish, not street food.

lunch.name: Kofte (Turkish Meatballs)
instructions: Kofte are the Turkish spiced meatballs or patties -- eaten across all of Turkey
Many regional variations: Inegol kofte (no breadcrumbs, distinct shape), Izmir kofte (baked with tomato and potato), Adana kofte (on a skewer, spicy)
The basic recipe: ground meat (lamb and beef) with onion, herbs, and spices
Shaped and grilled, pan-fried, or baked
Eaten with bread, rice, or salad
Turkish kofte variations are a map of regional identity
lunch.description: Turkish spiced meatballs -- ground lamb and beef with grated onion, parsley, cumin, and paprika, shaped and grilled, fried, or baked. Dozens of regional variations: Inegol (pressed, no breadcrumbs), Izmir (baked with potato and tomato), Adana (skewered, spicy). Kofte variations map Turkey's regional identity.

dinner.name: Kuru Fasulye (White Bean Stew)
ingredients: Lamb or beef (optional -- often just the beans)
instructions: Kuru fasulye is the Turkish national comfort food -- simple and profound
White beans cooked in a tomato-onion base until very soft
Often with lamb or beef but the vegetarian version is equally revered
Eaten over pilav (rice) or with bread
The dish of the traditional Turkish lokanta (canteen-style restaurant)
Associated with military service -- every Turkish man who did military service ate kuru fasulye
Voted among the most beloved Turkish dishes in national polls
dinner.description: Turkish white bean stew -- white beans slow-cooked in a tomato-onion base until very soft. Kuru fasulye (dry beans) is the Turkish national comfort food: the dish of the lokanta (canteen restaurant) and military service. Eaten over rice pilav. Simple, profound, deeply beloved.

dinner.name: Manti (Turkish Dumplings)
ingredients: Thin pasta dough (very thin -- the traditional manti are very small)
Ground lamb or beef, onion, parsley
Brown butter with dried mint and paprika
instructions: Manti are the Turkish dumplings -- the filling is tiny, the labor is immense
Traditional manti: very small, each the size of a small coin
The skill: 40 manti fitting on a single spoon is the Turkish grandmother benchmark
Filled with spiced ground meat
Boiled and served with a generous pool of garlic yoghurt
Drizzled with brown butter sizzled with dried mint and paprika
The combination: hot dumplings + cold garlic yoghurt + hot butter drizzle
Central Asian origin: related to Mongolian buuz, Chinese baozi, Korean mandu
dinner.description: Turkish tiny dumplings -- small pasta parcels filled with spiced lamb, boiled and served on a bed of garlic yoghurt with brown butter sizzled with dried mint and paprika. The traditional benchmark: 40 manti on one spoon (grandmother skill test). Central Asian origin: related to Mongolian and Chinese dumplings.

dinner.name: Imam Bayildi (Stuffed Eggplant in Olive Oil)
instructions: Imam bayildi means the imam fainted -- the name is the story
The story: the imam fainted from pleasure (or from the amount of olive oil used)
Eggplants are fried in olive oil, then stuffed with onion-tomato-garlic mixture
Slow-cooked until very soft and the olive oil is absorbed
Eaten at room temperature -- an olive oil vegetable dish (zeytinyagli)
Zeytinyagli dishes: Turkish vegetable dishes cooked in generous olive oil, eaten cold or room temperature
The olive oil is the flavor medium -- it absorbs all the aromatics
dinner.description: Turkish stuffed eggplant in olive oil -- eggplant fried, then stuffed with onion, tomato, and garlic, slow-cooked in generous olive oil until silky. Imam bayildi: the imam fainted (from pleasure, or from the olive oil). A zeytinyagli dish (olive oil vegetable): eaten at room temperature, the olive oil the flavor medium.

dinner.name: Adana Kebab
ingredients: Ground lamb (fatty -- from the tail fat)
Red chilli (Turkish biber -- fresh and dried, quite spicy)
Wide flat skewers (the kebab is hand-pressed onto the skewer)
instructions: Adana kebab is from the city of Adana in southern Turkey -- the spiciest region
Ground fatty lamb pressed onto wide flat metal skewers
Cooked over charcoal -- the fat drips and the flame chars the meat
Much spicier than Urfa kebab (the milder version from Sanliurfa)
The Adana-Urfa debate is a regional identity matter
Served with flatbread, grilled peppers, and sumac-onion salad
dinner.description: Turkish Adana spicy lamb kebab -- ground fatty lamb pressed onto wide flat metal skewers, chargrilled. Adana (southern Turkey, the spicier region): much spicier than Urfa kebab (the milder Sanliurfa version). The Adana-Urfa comparison is a regional identity matter. Served with flatbread and sumac-onion salad.

dinner.name: Pilav (Turkish Rice)
ingredients: Baldo or baldo-type rice (or orzo pasta for arpa sehriyeli pilav)
Chicken or vegetable stock (for cooking the rice in)
instructions: Turkish pilav is the foundation of Turkish cooking -- every meal has pilav
Made with butter, not oil -- this is the Turkish distinction
The rice is sauteed in butter first (the fried rice method)
Then hot stock added -- absorbed completely
The result: each grain separate, buttery, fragrant
Sehriyeli pilav: with orzo (small pasta) toasted in butter first -- the orzo turns golden-red, then the rice added
The toasted orzo gives crunch and a nutty contrast to the soft rice
dinner.description: Turkish butter-fried rice -- baldo rice sauteed in generous butter before stock is added, each grain separate and buttery. Sehriyeli pilav: with orzo toasted until golden-red before the rice goes in, the toasted pasta adding crunch and nuttiness. The foundation of Turkish cooking; every meal has pilav.

snacks.name: Borek (Pastry Rolls)
ingredients: Spinach and white cheese filling OR ground beef OR potato
Egg and oil or milk (for brushing)
instructions: Borek is the Turkish filled pastry -- the Ottoman pastry heritage
Yufka: the Turkish thin pastry, different from Greek phyllo (thicker, more doughy)
Many shapes: roll (sigara boregi -- cigarette), coil (su boregi), tray (tepsi boregi)
The most common fillings: spinach-white cheese, ground beef-onion, or potato
The Ottoman pastry tradition spread across the Balkans, Middle East, and North Africa
Su boregi (water borek): the yufka is briefly boiled before layering -- softer than regular borek
snacks.description: Turkish filled pastry -- yufka (Turkish thin pastry) filled with spinach and white cheese, ground beef, or potato, shaped into rolls (sigara boregi), coils, or trays. The Ottoman pastry heritage that spread across the Balkans and Middle East. Su boregi: the yufka briefly boiled before layering.

snacks.name: Ayran (Yoghurt Drink)
instructions: Ayran is the Turkish yoghurt drink -- drunk at every meal and available everywhere
Yoghurt diluted with cold water and salted
The salt is essential -- this is a savory drink, not sweet
Drunk with kebabs, kofte, bread, and all Turkish meals
Available in every supermarket, fast food restaurant, and kebab shop
The frothy top from whisking: the quality signal
Turkey exports ayran globally -- Ayran is the most consumed drink in Turkey after water
snacks.description: Turkish salted yoghurt drink -- yoghurt diluted with cold water and salted. Drunk with every Turkish meal. The frothy top from whisking is the quality signal. Savory, not sweet. Drunk with kebabs, kofte, and bread. Turkey's most consumed drink after water.

snacks.name: Midye Dolma (Stuffed Mussels)
ingredients: Spiced rice filling: short-grain rice, onion, pine nuts, currants, allspice, cinnamon, mint
instructions: Midye dolma are the Istanbul street food stuffed mussels
Large mussels stuffed with spiced rice (with pine nuts, currants, and warm spices)
The rice filling is the same style as Turkish dolma (stuffed vegetables)
Sold by midyeci vendors on the Istanbul waterfront -- especially Besiktas and Eminonu
Eaten in hand: the vendor opens the shell, you squeeze lemon, you eat from the shell
Bought by the tray -- you pay per mussel
snacks.description: Istanbul street food stuffed mussels -- large mussels filled with spiced rice (pine nuts, currants, allspice, cinnamon), steamed. Sold by waterfront vendors at Besiktas and Eminonu. The vendor opens the shell, you squeeze lemon, eat from the shell, buy by the piece. The taste of Istanbul street eating.

snacks.name: Simil and Beyaz Peynir (Simit with White Cheese)
ingredients: Beyaz peynir (Turkish white brine cheese -- similar to feta but milder)
instructions: Simit with beyaz peynir and cay is the Turkish working-class breakfast
The combination is so fundamental it is almost a cultural institution
Simit: crunchy, sesame-fragrant, slightly sweet from the pekmez glaze
Beyaz peynir: creamy, mild, briny -- a creamy white cheese in brine
Turkish cay (tea): small glass, strongly brewed black tea
This combination is eaten by millions every morning at the waterside, in parks, on commutes
snacks.description: Turkish classic breakfast combination -- simit (sesame bread ring), beyaz peynir (white brine cheese: milder and creamier than Greek feta), and cay (black tea in a small glass). Eaten by millions every morning. The fundamental Turkish working breakfast: crunchy-salty-sweet-hot.

desserts.name: Baklava
ingredients: Clarified butter (generously -- brushed on every layer)
Pistachios (Antep/Gaziantep pistachios -- the green Turkish pistachio)
Sugar syrup (cool, poured over hot baklava)
instructions: Turkish baklava is the pinnacle of Ottoman pastry art
The Gaziantep (Antep) pistachio: the bright green Turkish pistachio -- the best for baklava
Gaziantep has a protected geographical indication for its baklava
The technique: dozens of layers of paper-thin filo, each brushed with clarified butter
Cut before baking into diamond or square pieces
Baked golden, then cool syrup poured over hot baklava (or hot over cold -- the opposite creates a different texture)
The cool-over-hot rule: the temperature difference drives syrup absorption
Karakoy Gulluoglu and Hafiz Mustafa in Istanbul: the famous baklava houses
desserts.description: Turkish pistachio baklava -- dozens of paper-thin filo layers brushed with clarified butter, filled with Gaziantep pistachios (the bright green Turkish variety with GI protection), baked golden, cool syrup poured over hot. Gaziantep baklava has a protected designation. The pinnacle of Ottoman pastry craft.

desserts.name: Lokum (Turkish Delight)
instructions: Lokum (Turkish delight) was created in Istanbul in the late 18th century
Often attributed to Haci Bekir, a confectioner who came to Istanbul from Kastamonu around 1777
Haci Bekir's shop still exists in Istanbul (Eminonu)
Sugar and water cooked to a specific temperature, cornstarch added, stirred for hours
The long stirring creates the gel texture
Flavored with rosewater (the classic), mastic (resin from Chios mastic tree), or pistachio
European travellers in the Ottoman Empire discovered it and brought it back -- it became an exotic luxury in Victorian England
desserts.description: Turkish confectionery -- lokum (Turkish delight) created in Istanbul around 1777, attributed to Haci Bekir (whose shop still exists). Sugar and cornstarch cooked and stirred for hours into a gel, flavored with rosewater, mastic, or pistachio, cut and coated in icing sugar. European travelers spread it globally as an Ottoman luxury.

desserts.name: Sutlac (Rice Pudding)
instructions: Sutlac is the Turkish rice pudding -- served cold in earthenware pots
A very thin, creamy pudding -- more liquid than Western rice pudding
The firin sutlac (oven rice pudding) version: the top is browned under a very hot oven or grill
The burned top is the signature: browned, slightly caramelized
Eaten cold with the contrast of the warm (or cooled) burned top and cold creamy pudding
desserts.description: Turkish rice pudding -- sutlac, a thin creamy pudding served cold in earthenware pots. Firin sutlac: the oven version, the top browned under a hot grill into a caramelized crust. The burned top and cold creamy interior contrast is the signature experience.

drinks.name: Cay (Turkish Black Tea)
ingredients: Turkish black tea (Rize tea -- grown on the Black Sea coast)
instructions: Cay (pronounced chai) is the Turkish national drink -- consumed more per person than almost any other nation
Turkey has the highest per-capita tea consumption in the world
Grown on the Black Sea coast (Rize province) -- a relatively recent crop (1930s)
Before Rize tea, Turks drank coffee; Ataturk promoted tea after WWI to reduce dependency on imported coffee
Made in a double pot (caydanlik): water in the bottom, concentrated tea in the top
The tea is poured from the top pot (strong) and diluted with hot water from the bottom
Each person chooses their strength: koyu (dark) or acik (light)
Served in small tulip-shaped glasses with two sugar cubes
drinks.description: Turkish Black Sea tea -- cay brewed in a double pot (caydanlik: concentrated tea on top, hot water below for dilution), served in small tulip-shaped glasses. Turkey has the world's highest per-capita tea consumption. Rize province grows the tea. Ataturk promoted tea post-WWI to replace imported coffee.

drinks.name: Raki (Anise Spirit)
ingredients: Cold water (to dilute -- essential: turns white)
Ice (optional -- purists say ice first, then water)
instructions: Raki is the Turkish national spirit -- the Lion's Milk (aslan sutu)
Distilled from grapes and anise -- clear until water is added
The louche: the water turns the clear spirit milky white -- from the anise oils
This is why it is called the Lion's Milk -- the white cloudy appearance
Drunk very slowly at the raki table -- a meal in itself
The meze table: raki is drunk alongside many small dishes over hours
Yeni Raki is the most famous brand -- also Tekirdağ
The culture: drinking raki is an event, not just a drink
drinks.description: Turkish anise spirit -- raki (Lion's Milk: aslan sutu), grape-based spirit double-distilled with anise. Clear until water is added: the louche turns it milky white (anise oils suspending in dilution). Drunk slowly at a meze table over hours. Yeni Raki is the most known brand.

drinks.name: Salep (Winter Hot Drink)
ingredients: Salep powder (ground dried orchid tuber -- Orchis mascula and related species)
instructions: Salep is the Ottoman winter drink -- made from ground orchid tuber
The orchid tuber (from wild orchids of the Orchis genus) ground to a powder
Mixed with hot milk and sugar -- it thickens into a warming, slightly slimy drink
The characteristic texture: thicker than milk, slightly gel-like from the orchid starch
Traditionally sold by salep vendors in winter in Istanbul
The over-harvesting of wild orchids has made real salep rare and expensive
Much commercial salep now uses cornstarch substitutes
Cinnamon dusted on top is essential
drinks.description: Turkish Ottoman winter orchid drink -- salep powder (ground wild orchid tuber, Orchis genus) mixed with hot milk and sugar into a thick, warming, slightly viscous drink. Cinnamon on top. Over-harvesting has made real salep rare and expensive; most commercial salep uses cornstarch. Traditionally sold by winter street vendors in Istanbul.
